areas.title: Section 8: Gmail API technical architecture
areas.notes: Verified Section 8 (Gmail API technical architecture). All required OAuth scopes implemented: gmail.readonly, gmail.modify, gmail.labels, gmail.send (auth.config.ts:47-55). Bulk deletion uses batchDelete API with 1000 ID chunks as specified (client.ts:304-323). Token refresh persistence exceeds spec with automatic database updates on refresh (client.ts:69-128). Rate limit handling with exponential backoff for 429 errors (client.ts:240-252, 407-421). History API for incremental sync fully implemented (client.ts:366-446). InvalidTokenError class for graceful token revocation handling. Performance optimization: optional gmailClient parameter to avoid client churn. Security: header sanitization in sendEmail (client.ts:338-339).
improvements: Token refresh persistence to database with automatic updates on token refresh (spec only mentioned storing tokens)
Rate limit handling with exponential backoff retry logic (spec only documented limits, no handling strategy)
History API implementation for incremental sync (not mentioned in Section 8)
InvalidTokenError custom error class for graceful handling of revoked tokens
Optional gmailClient parameter to avoid per-message client churn (performance optimization)
Safe email sending with header sanitization to prevent injection attacks
Message headers normalization to key-value object for easier access

areas.title: Section 9: Detecting subscription emails
areas.notes: Verified Section 9 (Detecting subscription emails). Core detection algorithm implemented: List-Unsubscribe header (RFC 2369) with 95 confidence, RFC 8058 one-click with 100 confidence (detection.ts:25-58), List-Id header with 90 confidence (60-77), Precedence header (bulk/list/junk) with 75 confidence (79-97), 39 sender patterns vs 5 in spec (119-177), 19 ESP domains vs 3 in spec (179-217). Parse functions: extractEmailBody for multipart messages (253-291), parseBodyForUnsubscribeLink with spam filtering (297-336), parseMailtoUnsubscribe for mailto links (341-355), parseSender with lowercase normalization (227-247). REGRESSION: Gmail category detection missing - spec requires checking category:promotions and category:updates (spec line 87-88) but code doesn't check message.labelIds for CATEGORY_PROMOTIONS/CATEGORY_UPDATES.
improvements: Auto-Submitted header detection (99-117) - RFC 3834 standard not in spec's algorithm
39 sender patterns vs 5 in spec (newsletter@, noreply@, marketing@, updates@, plus 35 more: news@, digest@, notifications@, etc.)

ESP domain detection for 19 providers (Mailchimp, SendGrid, Substack, ConstantContact, Campaign Monitor, ConvertKit, Revue, Beehiiv, Sendinblue/Brevo, AWeber, ActiveCampaign, iContact, Emm.tf, MailerLite)
extractEmailBody() parses message body (HTML/plain text) with nested part handling for unsubscribe URLs
parseBodyForUnsubscribeLink() with spam phrase filtering (buy now, winner, urgent) and UTM parameter cleaning
parseMailtoUnsubscribe() extracts subject/body from mailto links for proper unsubscription emails
parseSender() normalizes emails to lowercase to prevent duplicate subscription groups
Confidence scoring more granular than spec (60-100 range with 60=auto-submitted, 65=ESP, 70=newsletter, 75=precedence, 90=list-id, 95=list-unsubscribe, 100=one-click vs binary true/false)
RFC 8058 one-click detection with List-Unsubscribe-Post header check (spec mentioned but algorithm didn't include)
regressions: Gmail category detection not implemented - spec explicitly lists checking for category:promotions and category:updates (spec line 87-88) as secondary detection signal, but detectSubscription() only receives headers parameter and doesn't check message.labelIds for CATEGORY_PROMOTIONS/CATEGORY_UPDATES labels

areas.title: Section 10: Automated unsubscription
areas.notes: Verified Section 10 (Automated unsubscription). RFC 8058 one-click implemented correctly with POST request, Content-Type header, and body 'List-Unsubscribe=One-Click' (unsubscribe.ts:13-39). Mailto unsubscribe implemented with parseMailtoUnsubscribe() extracting to/subject/body (detection.ts:341-355, unsubscribe.ts:44-65). HTTP unsubscribe with redirect detection (unsubscribe.ts:71-110) - detects 300-399 redirects but marks as manual. parseBodyForUnsubscribeLink() for fallback when no List-Unsubscribe header (detection.ts:297-336) with spam phrase filtering and URL validation. Error handling reports broken/expired links. REGRESSIONS: No CAPTCHA detection (spec line 126 requires flagging), no headless browser for confirmation pages (spec line 124 notes 'may require headless browser'). Covered by issue #130.
improvements: Spam phrase filtering in parseBodyForUnsubscribeLink() to avoid malicious URLs (detection.ts:307-321) - 'buy now', 'winner', 'urgent' etc.
URL validation with new URL() catch block prevents invalid URLs from being returned (detection.ts:324-329)
UTM parameter cleaning from URLs to avoid tracking parameters (detection.ts:317)
UnsubscriptionAttempt model tracks all attempts with status/error for audit trail (jobs.ts:352-359) - spec only mentioned reporting failure
90-day data retention cleanup for unsubscription attempts (jobs.ts:333-338) - privacy feature not in spec
Token refresh handling during unsubscription jobs via database fetch (jobs.ts:458-470) - spec didn't address token staleness
Comprehensive error messages distinguishing token errors from unsub failures (jobs.ts:400-412) - better UX than spec's 'report failure'
Safe email sending with header sanitization for mailto unsubscribe (client.ts:338-339) - security improvement
attemptUnsubscribe() supports all four methods: one_click, mailto, http, manual (unsubscribe.ts:115-148) - cleaner architecture than spec's implied approach
runUnsubscribe() skips unsubscription if method='none' with specific error message (jobs.ts:366-375) - graceful degradation
regressions: No CAPTCHA detection - spec Section 10 line 126 requires 'CAPTCHA protection → flag for manual user action', code accepts HTTP success (200/204/ok) without verifying actual unsubscription occurred (unsubscribe.ts:23-24, 94-96)

No headless browser for HTTP confirmation pages - spec line 124 notes 'HTTP unsubscribe shows confirmation page → may require headless browser', code returns 'manual action' message for redirects without attempting browser automation (unsubscribe.ts:83-89 comment acknowledges this)

areas.title: Section 11: Database schema
areas.notes: Verified Section 11 (Database schema). All 6 required tables implemented: subscriptions, subscription_preferences, gmail_sync_state, unsubscription_attempts, bulk_deletion_jobs, rollup_settings. Schema verified against prisma/schema.prisma and prisma/migrations/20250422000000_init/migration.sql. All foreign keys have CASCADE deletes (migration.sql:205-233). DeliverySlot enum correctly defined (migration.sql:4-5, schema.prisma:122-126). Field type mapping: spec VARCHAR(320) → Prisma @db.VarChar(320) for senderEmail (schema.prisma:71, migration.sql:59), BIGINT for historyId (schema.prisma:110, migration.sql:92).
improvements: Prisma cuid() for IDs instead of UUID v4 (schema.prisma:12,69,93,108,129,142,158) - more scalable, avoids monotonically increasing IDs that can cause index hotspots
Cascade delete behavior (onDelete: Cascade) on all 8 foreign key relations (schema.prisma:44,55,83,100,101,117,136,151) - spec didn't specify cascade behavior, code ensures automatic cleanup

Additional indexes beyond spec: Subscription.index([userId, lastSeenAt]) (schema.prisma:89), UnsubscriptionAttempt.index([status]) (schema.prisma:154), BulkDeletionJob.index([userId, status]) (schema.prisma:169)
User model extends spec with emailVerified field from NextAuth.js requirements (schema.prisma:14, migration.sql:11)
CamelCase field names (senderEmail, unsubscribeMethod) matching JavaScript conventions vs spec's snake_case - better code consistency
historyId nullable (BigInt?) in GmailSyncState (schema.prisma:110) vs required BIGINT in spec - more defensive for new users before first sync

areas.title: Section 13: Product architecture
areas.notes: Verified Section 13 (Product Architecture). All Phase 1 requirements implemented: Next.js 15+ with App Router, shadcn/ui + TailwindCSS, NextAuth.js v5, PostgreSQL + Prisma, BullMQ + Redis, googleapis. Workers use lazy-loading pattern within Next.js rather than separate services (pragmatic choice for smaller deployments). Five queues implemented vs three in spec (adds history-monitor for incremental sync, bulk-delete for cleanup operations).
improvements: Custom DashboardSkeleton implementation instead of shadcn/ui skeleton component (src/app/dashboard/page.tsx:119)
BullMQ workers run within Next.js app using lazy-loading pattern (src/modules/queues/queues.ts) - more flexible than separate services for smaller deployments
Additional history-monitor queue for incremental sync (src/modules/queues/queues.ts:69-77) - spec only mentioned email-scan, unsubscribe, rollup
Queue configuration with exponential backoff retry logic and automatic cleanup (src/modules/queues/queues.ts:7-21)
Five queues implemented: email-scan, unsubscribe, bulk-delete, rollup-digest, history-monitor (src/modules/queues/queues.ts)

areas.title: Unroll.me feature comparison (Section 2)
areas.notes: Verified Section 2 (Unroll.me feature comparison). How It Works page (src/app/how-it-works/page.tsx:123-175) contains comprehensive 'True Unsubscription vs Filtering' comparison section explicitly contrasting Prunebox vs Unroll.me. Landing page (src/app/page.tsx:98-106) includes 'Better than Unroll.me' section. README.md line 3 positions as 'better alternative to Unroll.me'. Implementation addresses all key spec points: Unroll.me's filtering-only approach (line 11-12), Uber scandal/data selling (lines 25-30), subscription detection explanation (lines 21-22), and user complaints (lines 32-38). How It Works page lines 89-121 explains detection algorithm with high/medium confidence signals matching spec. Privacy-first positioning throughout.
improvements: How It Works page provides user-facing Prunebox vs Unroll.me comparison with visual card layout (not in spec - spec was background research)
True Unsubscription vs Filtering section explicitly lists Unroll.me flaws (filtering only, subscriptions remain active, disconnecting floods inbox, sells data)
How We Detect Email Groups section explains algorithm to users with high/medium confidence signals (spec only documented detection for implementation)
Landing page 'Better than Unroll.me' section directly addresses Uber scandal (page.tsx:98-106)
Privacy guarantee section with Shield icon, no-data-selling pledge, Google Limited Use disclosure (how-it-works:177-195)
Rollup customization exceeds Unroll.me: 3 delivery slots vs 1, 14 timezones vs single, customizable digest name
Subscription list advanced filtering (high/low confidence, has unsubscribe, search by sender) exceeds Unroll.me capabilities
Confidence scoring system (0-100) for detection transparency not mentioned in Unroll.me spec
Bulk selection with checkboxes and select all functionality addresses spec complaint about Unroll.me (line 36)

areas.title: Legal compliance requirements (Section 12)
areas.notes: Verified Section 12 (Legal compliance requirements). All Google API Limited Use requirements implemented: no data selling (privacy:96), no advertising (privacy:97), no AI training (privacy:98), user data deletion enabled (settings:207-263, delete/route.ts:14-49). Privacy policy includes all required elements: data types (privacy:52-63), purpose (privacy:75-83), storage location (privacy:129), third parties (privacy:141-154), Limited Use disclosure (privacy:39-43). GDPR compliance: 72-hour breach notification explicitly stated (privacy:185), explicit consent via OAuth prompt:consent (auth.config.ts:44), right to erasure fully implemented with cascade deletion of all 8 tables. Only gaps are legal documentation (DPA, SCC) which are outside scope for self-hosted open-source model - covered by issue #92.
improvements: Data export API (/api/account/export) implements GDPR right to data portability beyond spec requirement
Privacy policy explicitly documents 72-hour breach notification with GDPR Article 33 reference (privacy:185-188)
Account deletion cascades through all 8 related tables with explicit deletion order (delete/route.ts:14-49) - spec only requires 'enable user data deletion'
GDPR rights section in privacy policy (access, rectification, erasure, portability, objection) goes beyond minimal spec (privacy:158-175)
Settings Privacy tab includes Google Limited Use disclosure for in-app transparency (settings:151-154)
Data export includes all user data: user profile, subscriptions, preferences, rollupSettings, syncState
Explicit opt-in consent via OAuth prompt:consent parameter (auth.config.ts:44) - spec requires 'explicit and opt-in (not pre-checked boxes)'
Gmail access revocation warning in settings (settings:115-118) with 'Coming soon' for revoke button
Privacy policy footer links to Terms and Home pages (privacy:220-224) for easy navigation
Terms page includes GDPR compliance clause for EU users (terms:175-176)

areas.title: Google verification process and timeline (Section 14)
areas.notes: Verified Section 14 (Google verification process and timeline). README.md lines 145-168 documents complete verification timeline: Brand verification (2-3 days), OAuth scope review (1-4 weeks), CASA Tier 2 assessment (1-3 weeks), Total 4-8 weeks minimum. CASA costs documented: Tier 2 ($500-1,000/year), Tier 3 ($4,500+/year), annual recertification required. Unverified consequences documented: 100 test user limit, 'Unverified app' warning, 7-day refresh token expiry. Privacy policy (/privacy) includes Google API Limited Use disclosure (line 39-42), all required elements: data types (headers, sender patterns), purpose (subscription management only), storage location/duration (PostgreSQL until account deletion), third parties (none for data use, Google OAuth for auth only), 72-hour breach notification. Terms page (/terms) exists with service description, user responsibilities, payment terms, liability limitations, governing law. OAuth scopes in auth.config.ts (lines 47-55) use full restricted scope URLs. DEPLOYMENT.md references verification requirements (line 42).
improvements: Verification timeline and costs documented in README.md with spec-exact table format (README:145-168)
Privacy policy includes all required Google verification elements: data types (headers, sender patterns), purpose, storage, third parties, Limited Use disclosure (privacy:39-43, 88-103)
Terms of service page exists and is accessible at /terms with GDPR compliance clause (terms:175-176)
OAuth implementation uses prompt: consent + access_type: offline for refresh token acquisition required for production (auth.config.ts:43-45)
Token encryption documented for CASA security requirements (README:98, DEPLOYMENT.md:62)

areas.title: Development timeline and budget (Section 15)
areas.notes: Spec Section 15 (lines 373-399) defines development timeline, compliance budget ($7,500-21,000 first year), and pricing tiers (Annual: $24.99/year, Monthly: $4.99/month, Lifetime: $59-79, Free tier: 10 unsubscribes). Codebase has COMPLETELY DIFFERENT business model: self-hostable open-source with NO pricing implementation. Evidence: README.md:5 'You can self-host your own instance', /pricing page linked in nav (how-it-works/page.tsx:47) does not exist, no Stripe/payment infrastructure, no pricing tables in Prisma schema, '10 free bulk deletions' claimed (how-it-works/page.tsx:200) but NOT enforced in code (bulk/route.ts only has technical limit of 100 per batch, no per-user quota tracking). Terms page mentions 'Free tier' and 'Paid tier' (terms/page.tsx:106-107) but no implementation exists. This is a SPEC GAP - spec assumes commercial SaaS, code implements open-source self-host. Existing issue #102 captures this drift as user-decision.
improvements: Core functionality ahead of spec timeline - all major features (scan, unsubscribe, rollup, bulk delete) implemented across Weeks 1-8 phases
Rollup implementation exceeds spec - supports multiple delivery slots (MORNING/AFTERNOON/EVENING, 14 timezones) vs spec's single delivery time mentioned elsewhere
Self-host open-source model addresses competitive gap mentioned in spec Section 6 (no competitor offers self-hosting option)
Docker deployment documentation (README.md:26-50, DEPLOYMENT.md) exceeds spec requirements for production readiness
regressions: Missing /pricing page - broken navigation link (how-it-works/page.tsx:47 links to non-existent page)
'10 free bulk deletions' marketing claim not enforced - bulk/route.ts:71-72,99-100 only limits 100 per batch technically, no per-user quota tracking database column or logic
Terms page references non-existent 'Free tier' and 'Paid tier' (terms/page.tsx:106-107) - confusing UX for self-host model
No usage metrics tracking - spec's free tier '10 unsubscribes' cannot be enforced without BulkDeletionJob usage aggregation

areas.title: Section 6: Competitive landscape and pricing strategy
areas.notes: Verified Section 6 (Competitive landscape and pricing strategy). Spec provides market research: feature comparison matrix (Clean Email $29.99/yr, Leave Me Alone, SaneBox $59-299/yr, Unroll.me free), market gaps (GDPR right to be forgotten, mobile-native, mass deletion, business features). Codebase has docs/CLEANEMAIL_COMPARISON.md with comprehensive 566-line competitor analysis. README.md:3, page.tsx:99-106, how-it-works/page.tsx:152 mention Unroll.me comparison. Fundamentally different business model: spec assumes commercial SaaS with pricing tiers, code implements self-host open-source. Issue #102 captures this SPEC GAP as user-decision.
improvements: Comprehensive CleanEmail comparison document (566 lines) covering feature parity, roadmap, implementation plans - exceeds spec research-only approach (docs/CLEANEMAIL_COMPARISON.md)
Self-host open-source model addresses competitive gap mentioned in spec line 150 (no competitor offers self-hosting option)
Open-source code provides auditability advantage not available to any competitor (comparison.md:443-447)
Zero subscription fees for self-hosted users vs all competitors charging $19-299/yr (comparison.md:433-451)
GDPR right to be forgotten (account deletion cascades all 8 tables) implements market gap from spec line 148

areas.notes: Verified Section 7 (Node.js technical implementation architecture). All spec-required technologies implemented: Next.js 15+ (package.json:49), shadcn/ui + TailwindCSS (Radix UI components:28-41, tailwindcss:69), NextAuth.js v5 (50), PostgreSQL + Prisma (prisma/schema.prisma:6-8), BullMQ + Redis (42, ioredis:47), googleapis (46). improvements: Additional bulk-delete queue beyond spec's three queues (queues.ts:25-26) - spec only mentioned email-scan, unsubscribe, rollup
History-monitor queue for incremental sync (queues.ts:69-77) - spec only documented future polling/push approaches as options

Queue configuration with exponential backoff retry logic and automatic cleanup (queues.ts:7-21) - spec only showed basic queue creation
Timezone-aware rollup scheduling with getUtcHourFromLocal helper (queues.ts:115-128) - spec showed hardcoded cron pattern
initializeHistoryMonitoringForAllUsers startup function (queues.ts:171-195) for automatic user monitoring - not mentioned in spec
